'''Pedron Niall''' (pronounced: PAY-drohn NEYE-awl) was the [[Lord Captain Commander]] of the [[Children of the Light]].

==Appearance==
He was a white-haired old man. His voice was thin and reedy with age. His body seemed all bone and sinew with thin skin like scraped parchment. Despite his age, there was nothing frail about him.

==History==
He was born in the year 911NE and took part in his first battle as a Whitecloak in 928NE.{{ref|Wheel of Time Companion}}

He was one of the [[Five Great Captains]].

He personally swore [[Geofram Bornhald]] into the ranks of the [[Children of the Light]] in {{Ne|962}}.

He instigated the beginning of the [[Whitecloak War]] in {{Ne|957}} by trying to expand into [[Altara]]. He won a number of battles against coalition forces led by [[Mattin Stepaneos den Balgar]] and even managed to capture him at the [[Battle of Soremaine]]. After ransoming Mattin back to Illian, Mattin managed to force the Whitecloaks to reaffirm the pre-war borders between Altara and [[Amadicia]].

During the [[Aiel War]], he was one of the more notable generals that made up the [[Grand Alliance]]. When the [[Aiel]] returned to the Waste, he held the army at the foothills of [[Kinslayer's Dagger]].

He was once married, but has been a widower for many years.{{ref/book|7|p}} His wife died before his rise to power.{{ref|Wheel of Time Companion}}

==Activities==
[[File:Pedron Niall.jpg|alt=Man on horse with flowing white cloak on green background|thumb|A young Pedron Niall from CCG.|left]]He was one of the first to realize that the [[Tarmon Gai'don|Last Battle]] was approaching but misinterpreted that he would be the leader of the forces of good and that they would all be under the banner of the Children of Light. He sent Geofram Bornhald to the [[Almoth Plain]] with a legion of Children of the Light. There he tried to put that area under Whitecloak control. From there he could have easier access to capture [[Arad Doman]] and [[Tarabon]], and put them under his control. He later sent [[Padan Fain]], under the command of [[Dain Bornhald]], to the [[Two Rivers]].

He committed treason by sending men to protect the [[Dragon Reborn]] in order for him to create chaos which Pedron would capitalize on to make his dream reality.{{ref/book|3|p}} He also gathered all other Children of the Light back to Amadicia.

He entered the Royal Palace of [[Amadicia]] to place [[Morgase Trakand]] under his protection. He promised to help Morgase take back [[Andor]] with his help. He also told her the news of [[Rahvin]] (Lord Gaebril) dying at the hands of the "false" Dragon, [[Rand al'Thor]]. This was all part of his plan to add Andor to his rule. She finally agreed to an alliance with Niall allowing the Children of the Light to be immune to Andor's laws when they finally ride into Andor. However he held back his invasion and also kept his men from attacking the [[Rebel Aes Sedai|Salidar Aes Sedai]].{{ref/book|6|31}}

He kept [[Galadedrid Damodred]] in the dark about Morgase being a "guest" in the Fortress of Light and sent [[Jaichim Carridin]] while he was acting as a diplomat in [[Ebou Dar]] to track down [[Elayne Trakand]] when she also arrived there.

He received confirmation about the [[Seanchan]] invading [[Tarabon]] but before he could do anything with this information he was killed by his spymaster, [[Abdel Omerna]], on [[Taisham 15]], {{Ne|1000}}.{{ref/book|7|p}}

He may have been bound to the wheel at his death, from indicators in ACOS Prologue. It describes Niall seeing "grey mist" and leading a charge, in addition to his memory fading. Heroes of the [[Horn of Valere]] can be new made from men and women who show uncommon heroism, according to [[Artur Paendrag Tanreall]]. Niall's status as a Great Captain and one of the most respected and feared men of the Third Age leads some to think that he will eventually reappear bound to the Wheel.
